iPhone 18 Pro and Pro Max will be in users' hands tomorrow (here's our review), and Apple plans to put the new devices to work immediately during this Friday's Friday Night Baseball broadcast — a Giants vs. Dodgers matchup. Here are the details.

Here's how Apple will use the iPhone 18 Pro during this Friday's Friday Night Baseball broadcast

Last fall, the iPhone 17 Pro made history as the first smartphone ever used to broadcast a professional sporting event. Four iPhone 17 Pros helped capture several unique game angles, and one of the used iPhones was subsequently inducted into the National Baseball Hall of Fame's collection in New York.

Now, riding the momentum of the iPhone 18 Pro launch, Apple plans to take things even further during this week's Friday Night Baseball.

Tomorrow night, Hong Kong time 10:15 a.m. on September 19 (local time), the final Friday Night Baseball broadcast of the season will deploy 14 iPhone 18 Pros to cover the San Francisco Giants hosting the Los Angeles Dodgers.

The iPhone 18 Pros will be positioned at several locations around Dodger Stadium, including the pitch clock, the netting behind home plate, the foul poles, and both teams' bullpens, giving viewers unique angles that traditional broadcast cameras can't capture.

Eight of the 14 iPhone 18 Pros will transmit live footage to the broadcast feed via a dedicated T-Mobile private 5G network. Beyond the game itself, the iPhone 18 Pros will also capture batting practice, player entrances, and moments inside the dugout.

Friday Night Baseball is available free for all Apple TV subscribers.

Apple TV costs $14.99 per month, and you can get a discount through the Apple One bundle.
